LQR gain K = [2.4146, 2.3264], x0 = (0.2, -0.1). LQR/MPC unconstrained first input (3 decimals)?
Why is the condensed QP strictly convex when R > 0?
options: Because Q is diagonal, which makes every term of the cost convex
H >= R I is positive definite, so the cost has a unique minimiser
Because the plant is stable, so the prediction matrices are bounded
Because the constraints are linear, which makes any quadratic cost convex
questions.explanation: Every term in H is positive semi-definite and R I is positive definite.

questions.prompt: A hard constraint on position is added and the cart starts too fast to stop in time. What happens?
options: The constraint is ignored automatically until the cart can stop
The solver silently returns the unconstrained LQR solution instead
The cart stops instantly, since the QP may exceed the input bound
The QP is infeasible: no input sequence satisfies all constraints
questions.explanation: Infeasibility is possible with state constraints; soft constraints and fallbacks are standard fixes.

questions.prompt: A very short horizon with terminal cost = stage cost causes an MPC cart to hover near but never reach the target. The most direct remedy is:
options: Make R exactly zero so the controller can use unlimited input effort
Remove the input constraint, keeping the same horizon and terminal cost
Use the Riccati matrix as terminal cost and/or lengthen the horizon
Increase the sample rate only, keeping the same horizon and terminal cost
questions.explanation: The terminal cost should represent the cost beyond the horizon.

questions.prompt: Which statement about clipping an LQR output at the actuator limit versus MPC is right?
options: They are identical, because clipping the LQR input is the same as solving a constrained QP
Clipping is always optimal, because the saturated input is the best feasible choice
MPC cannot use the same quadratic cost as LQR, so the two controllers cannot be compared
Clipping ignores the future effect of the limit; MPC plans around it and can be safer
questions.explanation: MPC optimises with the bound inside the problem.
